title: How should the landing be structured?
question: Fresh hand. The roll assigned a column of checks. Lock a composition, steer, or re-roll. KapeDoko’s coffee-bag world stays.

options.label: Column of checks
options.thesis: The fold is three stacked words — Hours, WiFi, Outlets — at display scale. The live reading is the only orange.
options.viewport: Sticky wordmark and Open the app. Filter your next brew. then three huge stacked lines: Hours Open now, WiFi Yes, Outlets Yes. Stamps sit under the column and reprint the values. Open the app is directly under the last line.
options.risk: A wall of type with no bag can feel like a manifesto, not a cafe tool, if the stamps disappear.

raised.raise: Each fact is a digit bank. Only the live reading glows orange; a stamp press cross-fades the value in place, like a tube changing depth.

options.label: Two-seat table
options.thesis: The fold is a cafe table: your stamps on one side, the shop’s bag on the other.
options.viewport: Filter your next brew. across the table. Left: Near You / Popular / WiFi / Plugs as place-setting stamps. Right: A work cafe bag that reprints. Open the app sits centered on the table edge. Compact stacks your stamps above the bag.
options.risk: A table metaphor can turn cute if plates or cutlery appear; keep it to stamps and one bag.

options.label: Queue card
options.thesis: You take a stamp like a queue ticket; the bag is the order now being called.
options.viewport: A short stub reads Now serving. The bag below is A work cafe with Hours, WiFi, Outlets. Tear-off stamps along the stub reprint the bag. Filter your next brew. is the ticket title. Open the app is Collect this shop.
options.risk: Queue chrome can feel like a cafe-game if Now serving gets cute or the CTA is renamed too far from Open the app.
